title: Billing Desk Calculation Sheet: HomeFlood Re-Rate Credit Amount
content:
**Calculation.** The re-rate credit on a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy is the pro rata amount described below. It is rounded to the cent once, at the end, and is never more than the net premium booked for the term.

**The fall.** The fall runs from the full-term premium booked as the term premium item for the term down to the certificate's re-rated term premium.

**The pro rata amount.** The fall is multiplied by the days from the date Tidemark received the certificate to the term end, and divided by the days from the term start to the term end.

**The ceiling.** The net premium booked for the term is its term premium item and its endorsement premium items, less the ENDORSEMENT and RERATE credits already given on it.

**Rounding.** Rounding to the cent takes the nearest cent; an amount lying exactly halfway between two cents goes to the even cent.

**Records read.**
- The certificate under review is the most recently received Elevation Certificate entry on the policy; where several share the latest receipt date, the one recorded first counts. It is read for the date Tidemark received it and its re-rated term premium.
- The term start, the term end and the premium items and credits of the term come from the policy and its premium ledger.

| Quantity | Source |
|---|---|
| full-term premium | term premium item booked for the term |
| re-rated term premium | the certificate entry under review |
| days remaining | receipt date of the certificate to term end |
| days in the term | term start to term end |
| ceiling | net premium booked for the term |

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

- A term premium item of 1,460.00 and a re-rated term premium of 1,095.00 give a fall of 365.00.
- In a 365-day term, the certificate was received with 120 days left to the term end.
- 365.00 multiplied by 120 and divided by 365 is 120.00. That is below the 1,460.00 booked for the term, so the re-rate credit is 120.00.
